headline: 05 entry + AFP wire) -- At least 40 Iranian sailors from US-sanctioned tankers anchored off Sri Lanka seek urgent medical
dek: At least 40 Iranian sailors from US-sanctioned oil tankers anchored just outside Sri Lanka's territorial waters have sought urgent medical treatment on the island, brought ashore through the port of Galle (115km south of Colombo) over the weekend. Sri Lanka's foreign ministry confirmed it…
sources: Sri Lanka foreign ministry spokesman Thushara Rodrigo, via AFP (carried by Gulf News, Straits Times, Free Malaysia Today, Khaleej Times)
fault_line: Blockade enforcement vs humanitarian obligation — should sanctioned crews be left stranded at sea while their ships sit in limbo?

sections.what_happened: At least 40 Iranian sailors from US-sanctioned oil tankers anchored just outside Sri Lanka's territorial waters have sought urgent medical treatment on the island, brought ashore through the port of Galle (115km south of Colombo) over the weekend. Sri Lanka's foreign ministry confirmed it coordinated the ship-to-shore transfer: 'We have coordinated the transfer and carried out our humanitarian obligations,' spokesman Thushara Rodrigo told AFP; costs borne by the Iranian embassy. Nearly a dozen empty Iranian tankers are anchored close to Galle harbour, in limbo because of the US blockade; Sri Lanka insists they sit in international waters. Context in the same report: a US submarine sank the Iranian frigate IRIS Dena nearby in March, killing 104 sailors; Sri Lanka's navy rescued 32; a second Iranian naval craft sought harbour at Trincomalee. Sri Lanka has deployed reconnaissance aircraft and patrol boats to monitor the vessels outside its 12-nautical-mile waters.
sections.what_verified: AFP Colombo reporting carried identically by Gulf News, Straits Times, Free Malaysia Today and Khaleej Times (one family, syndicated); on-record MFA spokesman statement inside the report
sections.what_disputed: Headcount discrepancy: AFP reports 'at least 40' sailors over the weekend, while a local Sri Lankan outlet (Gossip Lanka, no declared tier — not counted) reported 27 sailors brought ashore on the afternoon of Oct 24 by two navy patrol boats. The two figures may reflect different windows (one day vs the weekend) rather than a contradiction; the exact total is not settled. The nature of the sailors' illness is not stated in the AFP report.
sections.why_matters: The human edge of the blockade: sanctioned tankers parked off Galle, their crews coming ashore sick — the blockade's cost measured in sailors, not barrels.
